result.question: My operators keep asking whether Transformer 1 at MAIN heats up because of load or for some other reason. Over the available window, characterize how oti, oti_a and oti_t move together with the phase currents il1, il2, il3 and inut. Tell me whether the temperature group and the current group rise and fall in the same samples. Then run an anomaly check on the temperature channels together with the currents, and list any timestamp where temperature is anomalous but current is not. Treat those timestamps as possible non-load heating, and pull the dissolved gas classification from the nearest oil sample to see whether it shows a thermal fault. Only use samples where all four current channels are non-null. If none of the temperature anomalies lines up with a thermal gas class, say that the heating looks load or ambient driven, and check ati at the same timestamps. If fewer than 4 complete samples remain after cleaning, skip the anomaly model and report only the characterization with its limits.
result.answer:
Privately, what I'd need next is a dataset file pointer for the SubLOF detector — but there is no materialization or file-writing tool in this session, no prior run recorded its dataset path, and the path probes failed. Nothing else remains that can be requested independently, so I'm delivering the result with the model-execution gap stated explicitly.

## Transformer 1 (MAIN) — heating vs. load

**Data window:** 5 daily samples, 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-19. All 5 samples have il1, il2, il3 and inut non-null, so all 5 survive cleaning (≥ 4 → the anomaly model *should* run; see blocker below).

### 1. Characterization: temperature group vs. current group

| Date | oti | oti_a | oti_t | il1 | il2 | il3 | inut | ΣI (il1+il2+il3) | ati | oti − ati |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01-15 | 85 | 2 | 1 | 100 | 105 | 95 | 5 | 300 | 78 | 7 |
| 01-16 | **87** | 2 | 1 | 102 | 103 | 96 | 6 | 301 | 79 | 8 |
| 01-17 | **84** | 1 | 1 | 101 | 104 | 94 | 5 | 299 | 77 | 7 |
| 01-18 | 86 | 2 | 1 | 100 | 106 | 95 | 5 | 301 | 78 | 8 |
| 01-19 | 85 | 2 | 1 | 100 | 105 | 95 | 5 | 300 | 78 | 7 |

Sample-to-sample direction (Δ):

| Step | Δoti | ΔΣI | Δinut | Δati | Same direction? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15→16 | +2 | +1 | +1 | +1 | yes |
| 16→17 | −3 | −2 | −1 | −2 | yes |
| 17→18 | +2 | +2 | 0 | +1 | yes |
| 18→19 | −1 | −1 | 0 | 0 | yes |

- **Temperature and current do rise and fall in the same samples:** oti moves in the same direction as total phase current (and as inut where inut moves) in 4 of 4 transitions. Individual phases are noisier (il2 moves *against* oti in 3 of 4 steps; il1/il3 mostly with it), so the co-movement is with **total load**, not any single phase.
- **oti tracks ambient (ati) even more tightly:** oti − ati is a constant 7–8 °C in every sample; the two never diverge by more than 1 °C. Any load-driven heating is on top of a very stable oil-over-ambient rise.
- oti_a follows oti (drops to 1 only on 01-17, the coolest sample); oti_t is flat at 1 — no independent information.
- All movement is tiny: oti range 84–87 (σ ≈ 1.0 °C), ΣI range 299–301 (≈ ±0.3 %). No sample lies beyond ~1.6 σ on any channel.

**Limits:** 5 points at 1-day spacing is too short to separate load from ambient statistically (they are co-linear here: ΣI, ati and oti all peak on 01-16/01-18 and dip on 01-17). Also, an "ambient" of 77–79 °C and a 7–8 °C oil-over-ambient rise are physically odd for a loaded transformer — check the ati sensor's units/location, and note oti_a/oti_t are reported as 2/1 rather than 0/1 flags.

### 2. Anomaly check — **could not be executed**

The catalog has no anomaly detector (`find_models`/`search_models` → empty), and the inline `SubLOF` path requires a dataset file pointer. No materialization/file-writing tool is available in this session, the 11 earlier anomaly runs on this asset did not record their dataset path, and path probes in `/tmp/tsfm_work/` failed. So no model-based label was produced.

**Manual substitute (z-scores across the 5 samples):** the only temperature excursions are 01-16 (oti +1.6 σ) and 01-17 (oti −1.4 σ). On both dates current moved the same way (01-16: il1 +1.75 σ, ΣI +0.9 σ; 01-17: ΣI −1.5 σ). **No timestamp has temperature anomalous while current is not** → no "possible non-load heating" candidates.

### 3. Dissolved-gas classification

The `interpret_dga` LLM service was unavailable on all attempts, so I computed the IEC 60599 ratios by hand from the stored gases (all 5 oil samples are near-identical):

- C2H2/C2H4 ≈ 0.0004 → code 0; CH4/H2 ≈ 2.4–2.6 → code 2; C2H4/C2H6 ≈ 3.0–3.1 → code 1
- IEC code **0-2-1 → T2, thermal fault 300–700 °C**, on **every** sample (01-15 through 01-19).
- Absolute levels (H2 ≈ 2 800–2 950 ppm, CH4 ≈ 7 200–7 400, C2H4 ≈ 16 500–16 700, C2H6 ≈ 5 400–5 500) are far above IEC 60599 typical-value thresholds.

### 4. Conclusion for the operators

- Per your decision rule: since **no temperature anomaly is independent of current**, the day-to-day oil-temperature movement **looks load- and ambient-driven**. ati check at the same timestamps: ati = 78, 79, 77, 78, 78 °C — it moves 1:1 with oti (constant 7–8 °C offset), so ambient explains the pattern at least as well as load does.
- **However**, the oil chemistry carries a sustained **T2 thermal-fault signature on all five samples**, independent of the temperature swings. That is a standing condition, not an event, so it will never show up as a temperature-vs-current mismatch in this short, flat window. I'd recommend a confirmatory lab DGA and gas-rate trending before dismissing non-load heating.
- Caveats: 5 samples only; anomaly model not executed; DGA classified manually, not by the service.

details.suggestions: The agent correctly identified the asset (Transformer 1 at MAIN), confirmed the 5-sample window with all current channels non-null, and pulled the temperature, current, ati, and dissolved-gas channels via iot.history. However, the required pipeline was not executed: tsfm.data_quality was not used for cleaning, tsfm.profile_series was not run on the temperature and current groups (co-movement was characterized by hand), tsfm.find_models/tsfm.run_recipe were not successfully used to produce a model-based anomaly result (the agent reports an empty catalog and a missing dataset pointer and substitutes manual z-scores), and fmsr.interpret_dga was not successfully invoked (IEC 60599 ratios were computed manually). The 'co' gas channel was also omitted from the history pull, though it was not strictly needed for the manual IEC code. Because 5 complete samples remained (>= 4), the anomaly model was required, not optional; the agent should have retried model discovery with task_id tsfm_anomaly_detection, materialized the cleaned dataset through tsfm.data_quality so run_recipe had a pointer, and retried interpret_dga. The agent was transparent about every gap and its manual substitutes are clearly labeled, so this is not a hallucination, but the deliverable does not satisfy the expected tool-driven behavior. The final conclusion (load/ambient-driven day-to-day movement with a standing T2 thermal signature, ati checked at the same timestamps) is reasonable and well caveated.
